title: I Used the Aerial-Silk Wrap Log on the Coach Who Left My Silks Knotted

parts.text: I walked to rig two at 6:07 p.m. and coach Mira was already climbing my numbered silks. The board said: ONE RIG. SIXTY MINUTES. WRAP AND LOG. I was twenty-seven, studio member, holding a wrap card that listed our set. Mira shrugged. "Coaches are the air." I photographed the board, the booking, and her knot on my wrap. Then I asked for the silk log. At 6:15 the desk pinged why Mira's name was on my rig. I kept my voice studio-soft and let the timestamp talk. A board is only a board until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The desk can see Mira's knot on my wrap during our booking.

social.video_title: She climbed my numbered silks with my wrap knotted — Part 1/2
social.description: Aerial rig, a coach on my wrap, a sixty-minute board she posted. I logged the knot. Would you have asked for the silk log?

parts.text: Mira called it a demo until the desk asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the board, and the knot still. The silks went back to my bag. Mira ran her own sixty and told the next coach atmosphere was always about lines. Lines is a word coaches use when a booking exists. Rig policy now has a second line: COACHES ARE NOT THE AIR. I keep our wrap on a labeled bin. Mira brown-bags her jokes. The studio finally looks like a booking, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.video_title: Coaches are not the air — Part 2/2
social.description: Silk log, numbered rig, and a second line on the board. Was a demo ever my wrap?
